Analysis.object: Gender role stress (GRS) and sociocultural influences are impoortant correlated of muscle dysmorphia. Physical unattractiveness explained the greater variance in muscle dysmorphia symptoms of both Female and male. MD symptoms for male were associated with seeing beautiful Female or handsome male in movies, TV, or ads. MD symptoms in male were not related to remarks by male friends or remarks by Female friends. Remarks from male friendss and strangers were more predictive sociocultural influences of MD for Female.

There was no measure of participants gender role identification. The assessment tools used to measure such haracteristics are inherently problematic. Absent from the discussion of the results are comments about the relative importance of individual scale items. It would be impossible to make meaningful judgmalets about the theoretical contributions of individual subscale items or even overall subscales scores to MD symptoms. The limited age range and lack of racial diversityin our sample restricted our ability to make conclusions about a broad segmalet of the population. We did not assess participants sexual orientation, further restricting the generalizability of our results. The level of MD reported in our sample was rather low.

Population.object: Female and male undergraduate students from a large northwestern university
